versions.changelog: Metadata only: set topics (ai-workflow,adversarial-review); categories unchanged. No content change.
Metadata only: set categories (Development, Agents). No content change.
Rename: debate is the new name; the old slug redirects here. Package name and self-references updated, no behaviour change.

Removes the handoff/DeepSeek channel. It launched the external model with permission prompts off, so that model could run commands as the user, which the staging-directory flow could not contain; removing it also removes the skill's only install instruction (it now states that it installs nothing). Two read-only channels remain: Codex CLI (read-only sandbox) and Cursor CLI (plan mode). Any channel added later must be read-only, resumable, and startable from an explicit directory.

Root every attacker channel in the staging directory: cursor-agent and the handoff dispatcher now carry an explicit starting-directory flag like the Codex command already did, and the text no longer calls a starting-directory flag a jail. Also discloses that the handoff channel is not read-only (its backends run with permission prompts off) and that 'handoff run --dry-run' prints the backend's credentials.

Disclosure and dependency fixes from the security audit. The skill now says plainly that source files you attach are sent to the external vendor too and stay in that vendor's session history, and step 1 puts a per-vendor, per-file confirmation, a staged directory, a secrets scan and a record in front of any file being sent (brief-only is the default). The P3 install line now names the real PyPI package (handoff-cli, not the unrelated 'handoff'), an exact version, the index and an artifact hash. The description opens with a warning; the 'writes nothing' claim is reconciled with step 6.

Methodology upgrade, not just wording. R1 objections now require a verifiable anchor (file:line, runnable command, citable data) plus a mandatory closing question: what's the failure scenario for NOT acting. R2 rulings carry an evidence tag - verified / reasoned / to-verify - and only verified items are consensus-eligible. R3 no longer forces a consensus list: it outputs three categories (still disputed / unresolved-no-evidence-either-side / verified consensus), and failing to converge is not treated as a failure. R4 fresh judge is now mandatory whenever a trigger fires (a prohibition in the consensus, zero rejections all session, or 5+ consensus items) instead of optional. Core stances gained a hard number: across an archived sample, only ~1 in 40 objections was actually rejected, and every real rejection came from running production data - a warning against mistaking agreement for a working debate. New closing-handoff step: standalone use has no outer process to catch the consensus, so the session must propose where each verified item lands and wait for confirmation, flagging anything unconfirmed rather than dropping it silently. Also fixed: a shell-quoting pitfall where a prompt containing backticks breaks command substitution unless piped through a heredoc first.

Dropped the keyword list from the description, stopped naming an unpinned install command, and added a 'What this skill sends where' section: the brief is transmitted verbatim to another vendor's model, nothing else leaves the machine, and no key is ever handled by the skill.
P3 is executable again: the handoff CLI is a public package (uv tool install handoff-cli), and its resume subcommand keeps R1 and R3 on one conversation, which is exactly what this channel requires.
Full English rewrite. Same protocol, same channel ladder, same hard-won pitfalls (Codex resume flag order, Cursor CreatePlan swallowing output) - only the language changed.

Adversarial-debate skill v1.0.0 — Initial Release

- Enables cross-vendor adversarial debate: proposals are challenged by models from other vendors, with consensus reached via multi-round review.
- Initiates only when users explicitly request ("辩论一下", "让另一家模型打一打", "对抗评审"); does not activate for internal roundtable (self-dialogue) debates.
- Three-round protocol: attack from external model, user-side defense/judgment, and consensus formation; optional fourth round with a fresh, independent judge for major proposals.
- Clear separation between meta-requests (about the skill itself) and actual debate requests.
- Detailed procedures for proposal preparation, attack, defense, consensus, and judge roles; safeguards against process pitfalls and over-engineering.
- Model/channel selection guidelines ensure true cross-vendor involvement; built-in protocol for channel health checks and fallback.
